en: Itivuttaka 15: Ekakanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after speaking these words, he did so because he had something further to say. What, friends, is that which the Blessed One had further to say? 'Friends, there is one thing that, if practiced and cultivated, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. And what is that one thing? Mindfulness directed to the body (kāyagatāsati). Friends, this is that one thing that, if practiced and cultivated, leads to the complete destruction of suffering.

This is what the Blessed One had further to say, friends. For this reason, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after speaking these words. Then the Venerable Ānanda, having understood the meaning of this, recited these verses: "The Teacher has taught the Dhamma well; For those who practice it, there is no sorrow. Mindfulness directed to the body, Developed and cultivated, Leads to the complete destruction of suffering. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. The Discourse on the Fetter of Craving.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, I do not see even a single fetter, bound by which beings wander and transmigrate for a long time, comparable to this, bhikkhus: the fetter of craving."
“Bhikkhus, it is because they are fettered by the fetter of craving that beings wander and transmigrate for a long time.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
a person wanders through the long course of existence,
from this state of being to another state of being.”
that craving is the origin of suffering—
“Free from craving, without grasping, let the mindful bhikkhu wander forth.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
